title: Dual-write: every Item writer keeps headStageKey on the head row only
description: One helper (content_item_lifecycle.head_stage_fields) returns {headStageKey: stage} for the row being made head and {headStageKey: None} for the row being superseded; every writer that sets stage or versionState uses it in the write it already makes: publishing.save_item (create), publishing.publish_item (head and the sibling supersede loop), publishing.unpublish_item, story_reporting.save_story_version (create and supersede), story_reporting.move_story_stage, repair_story_versions, content_item_lifecycle create/assignment, assignments_workflow Item upserts, copywriting, story_triggers, editor_review, story_selection, story_commands, seed_edition, markus_import. No extra write and no extra read per save. The authoring client checks once per process that the site's Item type has headStageKey (graphql_type_field_names) and drops the field when it does not, so a new CLI still works against a site not yet deployed. A test-only invariant (fake client) asserts after every backend scenario that each lineage has at most one row with headStageKey and that it equals that row's stage. Acceptance: Gherkin writer scenarios pass; invariant hook on; writes per save unchanged (asserted by the request meter).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Dual-write in https://github.com/AnthusAI/Papyrus/pull/1364: head_stage_key/head_stage_fields (Python), contentItemHeadStageKey (TS). Key present when the row is not superseded (current, draft or none) and has a stage: on MoM 15 of 259 stories have only a draft row. Supersede clears the key and passes the row's own updatedAt (finding confirmed: 180 of 629 superseded rows on MoM have updatedAt within 10 s of the next version's creation). Invariant runs after every backend scenario. The CLI leaves the field out on sites without it (checks once, says so once). CI green.
